messages:
Charu: FYI repro of a weird KV divergence on magnetX-quant4 during coldstart. Seen after ~6k tokens when prefill >2k. Dumped cache fingerprints and the index looks skewed, not a simple off-by-one. Sharing minimal repro below.

Dmitri: Can you paste the exact run command and quant flags?

Charu: Sure —
```bash
python run_infer.py --model magnetX-13B-quant4 --quant-mode int4v2 --prefill 2500 --sequence 8000 --batch 1 --seed 42
```
Also attached the two cache dumps (fingerprint + indices) to the ticket.

Eva: Reproduced locally on my 80GB machine. Behavior differs if I run with --warmstart true vs false. Warmstart=true looks stable. Warmstart=false shows the token drift around token ~6150. :eyes:

Ben: Interesting. I tried toggling rotary scaling to 0.99 and 1.01 — no change. Could be a handshake timing issue between shard init and kv base pointer.

Dmitri: Can you dump the raw KV index values right after prefill and then every 512 tokens? I want to see whether the skew appears abruptly or drifts.

Charu: Done. Put the CSVs in /tmp/magnetX-coldstart-debug. Quick observation: the index values look consistent across shards until the first long-attention flush, then one shard's indices increment incorrectly by +16.

Alice: I pushed a tiny patch that forces a per-shard handshake re-sync after prefill: github.com/redwood/repro/commit/af3d9c (small change, adds barrier + memzero on offset table). Can someone try it?

Ben: Running with Alice's patch now on int4v2. Initial run: no divergence up to 9k tokens (single run). Will run a looped stress overnight.

ci-bot: build/1428 started for branch charu/magnetx-coldstart-patch — logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/build/1428 

Eva: Quick micro-test: zeroing the per-shard offset after prefill mitigates the issue but introduces a small latency spike (~3ms/token). So it's a plausible workaround but not ideal perf-wise.

Dmitri: Could be that quantized memcpy pads are misaligned and only surface after long sequences. Charu, can you try the same repro with quant-mode=int4v2 but with explicit alignment pad turned off (ALIGN_KV=false)?

Charu: Will run that next. If ALIGN_KV toggles it, then we have a memcpy/alignment bug. If not, it's likely an async handshake race.

Ben: FYI the patch Alice made also added an assertion that caught a rare condition where shard A reported base_index==0 while the global counter was 16k — assertion triggered once in my loop.

Alice: That assertion was the clue I needed. I also added a diagnostic metric (kvcache.retxn.mismatch) to the test build. Pls watch the console.

Charu: ALIGN_KV=false result: still reproduces, but the onset token shifted slightly (~6020). So alignment matters a bit but doesn't fully explain it.

Dmitri: OK narrowing: triggers only when (1) prefill >2k, (2) warmstart=false, (3) quant=int4v2 and (4) stream_mode=continuous. That combo reduces search space.

Eva: Logged a short regression test in the longctx-suite with those exact flags. test id: longctx/kv-coldstart-058. Will run on the canary pool.

Ben: Overnight stress with Alice's re-sync patch so far looks good. If green in morning, we can consider adding a guarded re-sync only for coldstart cases.

Charu: Thanks all. I'll collect the traces and draft a short postmortem note if overnight run passes. If not, I'll drop a bisect plan. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: build/1428 completed: SUCCESS. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/1428/kvcache-diagnostics.tar.gz

Alice: If patch is green, I'll open a small PR to add an opt-in resync flag behind a runtime env var so Dedicated customers don't see latency by default.

Dmitri: Good plan. Also add a unit test that simulates staggered shard init to avoid regressions.

Charu: Agree. Leaving this thread — will update with morning results. Thanks team. :party_parrot:
